attributes.experience:
Cexplorer.io (formerly Adapools) has been live since 2020, serving over 50,000 monthly users and handling millions of data requests each month.

- The team has strong experience in backend systems, frontend development, API design, and DevOps, specifically tailored to Cardano’s architecture (e.g., DB-Sync, Cardano Node, CIPs).
- Proven ability to maintain high availability, fast performance, and implement continuous improvements based on real user feedback.
- The team is fully equipped to ensure long-term support, stability, and delivery of new features in a rapidly evolving ecosystem.
attributes.proposal_name: Cexplorer.io – Developer-Focused Blockchain Explorer for Cardano
attributes.key_dependencies:
This proposal has no major external dependencies and can begin immediately upon funding. However, the following ongoing inputs are essential for continued success:

- Access to reliable Cardano node and DB-Sync services

- Timely updates from the Cardano core and tooling ecosystem (e.g., new protocol versions, CIP implementations)

- Stable API access to third-party services (e.g., market data for token pricing)

All technical and operational dependencies are already managed internally by the Cexplorer.io team.
attributes.maintain_and_support:
Cexplorer.io is already live and actively maintained by an experienced team of backend, frontend, and infrastructure developers. This proposal includes funding for ongoing maintenance, including server infrastructure, performance monitoring, bug fixes, and updates aligned with Cardano protocol changes.

The platform will continue to be supported by the same team, with a focus on long-term sustainability. Future updates will be driven by community needs, ecosystem growth, and emerging standards (e.g., new CIPs). Usage metrics, user feedback, and ecosystem developments will guide our roadmap to ensure Cexplorer remains a reliable and evolving resource.
attributes.proposal_description:
Cexplorer.io is a high-performance, feature-rich blockchain explorer designed specifically for the Cardano ecosystem. It offers deep on-chain insights, real-time data access, and powerful tools for developers, stake pool operators, and users. With over 50,000 monthly users and millions of processed data requests, Cexplorer.io has become a trusted resource in the Cardano community.

This proposal seeks funding to ensure the long-term sustainability of the platform through infrastructure maintenance and continuous improvement. It includes two key areas:

BAU/Maintenance – Covering costs for server infrastructure, backend/frontend development, and bug fixes to ensure stability, uptime, and security.

Enhancements & New Features – Expanding the team with additional developers and a UI designer to deliver a better user experience, improved performance, and new developer-oriented features.

Our mission is to provide a scalable, developer-friendly explorer that empowers the Cardano community with transparent, accessible, and actionable data. By supporting this proposal, Intersect and the broader community invest in critical infrastructure that enhances transparency, encourages innovation, and reduces friction for anyone building on or interacting with Cardano.
attributes.key_proposal_deliverables:
This proposal is focused on two parallel tracks: maintaining the stability of the current platform (BAU) and delivering meaningful enhancements. The deliverables and target outcomes for this tranche include:

1. BAU / Maintenance
- Continuous uptime of core services (>99.9% availability)
- Timely updates aligned with Cardano protocol changes (e.g., new eras, hard forks)
- Bug fixes, security patches, and performance optimizations
- Scalable infrastructure management (servers, DB, APIs)

Definition of Done:
Ongoing, stable operation of Cexplorer.io with no major service interruptions, tracked monthly.

2. Enhancements / New Features
- Deployment of 2–3 major feature updates (e.g., improved address/token views, expanded smart contract data, UX/UI refinements)
- Integration of a UI/UX designer to improve usability and visual clarity
- API enhancements and better developer-facing tooling

Definition of Done:
Public release of new features on the live platform, with changelogs and announcements, within the funding period.
attributes.resourcing_duration_estimates:
Team Size:
- 2 Backend Developers (1st full time, 2nd full/part-time)
- 1 Frontend Developer
- 1 UI/UX Designer (part-time)
- 1 DevOps / Infrastructure Support (part-time)
- 1 Project Coordinator (part-time)

Duration:
12 to 18 months – covering both ongoing maintenance and delivery of new features as outlined.

attributes.problem_statement: The Cardano ecosystem lacks a powerful, developer-friendly explorer with advanced features, real-time insights, and flexible tools for building on-chain apps. Cexplorer.io aims to fill this gap by providing deep data access, improved UX, and ongoing enhancements to support the growing needs of users and developers.
attributes.proposal_benefit: Cexplorer.io serves over 50,000 monthly users and processes millions of data requests, providing real-time, in-depth insights into Cardano’s blockchain. It supports developers, SPOs, researchers, and everyday users with tools for exploring transactions, addresses, tokens, and stake pools. By improving transparency and accessibility, it reduces friction in dApp development, stake pool monitoring, and ecosystem analysis. The return on investment is a proven, high-traffic platform that continuously evolves to meet the growing demands of the Cardano community.

attributes.comment_text:
Not sure if "help my failing business model" due to being unable to keep up with necessary changes to remain relevant and competitive, is an appropriate usecase for the Treasury. 
You say "Meaningful enhancements" under which you list "updates aligned with Cardano protocol changes (e.g., new eras, hard forks)" - something that happened months ago and you missed to care about. 
"Bug fixes, security patches, and performance optimizations" and "Continuous uptime of core services" is default behaviour for any service. Im sorry, but if this needs funding, you have no idea what you are doing. 

Imagine if every company asks the Treasury for funding basic operations. Or at the very least.. Will we now pay all explorers 150k a year? 

Further... 
1. As the treasury funds your operations, will cexplorer.io also be ad-free following acceptance of this proposal? 
2. Will cexplorer.io always rely on subsidies going forward?
3. Is there any guarantuee that cexplorer.io will remain operational and accessible after funding? Especially for the mentioned time span of 18 months. 
4. How do we know the mentioned "developer-focussed" features are unique, and valuable and not just keeping up with cardanoscan and ada.stats? 
5. Does "maintenace" in your timeline suggest that you catch up with Governance in the first 3 months? And start on the vaguely mentioned new features afterwards?

With regards to transparency, I've asked on several ocassions over the years for them to disclose the details of their "native" pool rankings (that they show on site as well as serve up via APIs to some of the wallets, that seem to disproportionally favour some of their own pools and possibly their paying client base) but have been ignored / blocked. While they do have some useful data collation pages on their site and provide some educational articles from time to time, this requested amount seems like a bit much given the amount of improvements I've seen to the site over the past year or two. (also worth noting Cardanians group have ~6 stake pools and Cardano Foundation delegation currently, collecting ~ 17.5k Ada in pool fees per calendar month.)

Questions about Business Model and Sustainability

1. What business model have you been operating under since your launch in 2020?
2. After this funding of 266,667 ADA, do you have specific plans to establish sustainable operations without additional support from the treasury in the future?
3. Could you provide a breakdown of your current revenue streams (advertising, paid API plans, stake pool operations, etc.) and explain what percentage of your operating costs they cover?
4. What is your funding strategy to ensure continuous operation of the service after the 18-month funding period ends?
5. How many monthly active users and what level of API usage do you believe are necessary for the project to become financially self-sufficient?

Questions about Community and Governance

1. How do you collect and incorporate feedback from the community into your product development?
2. How do you address the potential conflict of interest between your role as a stake pool operator and your role as an explorer service provider?

I appreciate the value Cexplorer.io brings to the Cardano ecosystem — especially its depth of data and developer-focused features, which in my view still stand out compared to other explorers like Cardanoscan or AdaStat.

For that reason, I am generally supportive of this proposal. Losing free access to Cexplorer or seeing it move to a paid model would likely create friction for many developers and SPOs who rely on it.

However, I would like to understand the long-term sustainability plan.
Will Cexplorer continue to rely on treasury funding in the future, or is there a roadmap toward becoming self-sustaining?
Clarifying this point would help ensure the project aligns with the broader goal of building resilient infrastructure for Cardano.

Thank you for the great work so far, and I look forward to your response!

Thank you for the kind words and for recognizing the role Cexplorer plays in supporting developers and SPOs. You're absolutely right — free access is a core part of our mission, and we fully agree that introducing barriers would create friction, which we want to avoid. Our long-term goal is self-sustainability, and this proposal is a bridge to get us there.

Right now, the platform is supported through a minimal advertising model, which helps cover basic infrastructure but doesn’t allow for real improvements. This proposal gives us the runway to reduce ads even further, continue offering free API access, and invest in the feature development the community expects.

Post-funding, our plan is to introduce light monetization options — for example, optional paid API tiers or non-intrusive sponsorships — aimed at professional users who need higher throughput or advanced tooling, without impacting casual access or the core features of the platform.

We are absolutely committed to keeping Cexplorer open and accessible, and our roadmap is designed to support that while building toward financial independence from the treasury.

In short:

a) This proposal buys us time to grow sustainably
b) Free access will remain a priority
c) And yes — we’re actively working toward a self-sustaining model
I am curious about this now as well.

Considering many of the other proposals in core are literally asking for funding basis operations, it is a question of where the line is drawn between acceptable and unacceptable. We really need a values based metric on how to view requests like this.

Business Model and Sustainability:

1. Since 2020, we have operated Cexplorer.io under a minimal advertising model. Our main income comes from light on-site ads, designed to be as unobtrusive as possible. We have kept all data access and APIs free to maximize value for developers, SPOs, and the community.

2. Yes. The primary purpose of this funding is to give us the runway to transition toward self-sufficiency. After the 18-month period, we plan to:
a) Minimize ads even further during the funded period
b) Introduce optional paid API plans for high-volume users
c) Explore light partnerships and sponsorships
d) We intend to sustain operations independently without needing ongoing treasury support.

3. Advertising: ~80% of revenue (small banner ads). Stake pool operations: 20% of revenue (variable). No paid APIs yet. Together, these revenue streams currently cover around 70–80% of basic infrastructure costs, but are not enough to fund full development or scaling.

4. Our post-funding strategy includes: 
a) Continuing cost optimization on infrastructure
b) Introducing optional paid APIs for enterprise or high-traffic users
c) Keeping basic access free to avoid friction for developers and SPOs
d) Growing user engagement to organically increase sustainability opportunities
We are committed to balancing accessibility and financial stability carefully.

5. At around 80,000–100,000 monthly active users and with a modest conversion rate to optional paid API usage, Cexplorer.io can become fully self-sustaining.
Currently, with approximately 30,000-50,000 monthly users, we cover basic running costs but can't grow without external funding.

Community and Governance:

1. We actively collect feedback through GitHub issues and feature requests, Direct feedback via X (formerly Twitter) and email, Monitoring platform usage to understand needs, and listening to SPO and developer communities.
Many past improvements, such as enhanced token views and faster API responses, were directly based on user feedback.

2. We take neutrality seriously. Our explorer does not promote any specific pool, including our own. All stake pool data and rankings are transparent, filterable, and based on public, objective blockchain data. We intentionally designed Cexplorer to allow users to set their own criteria for pool evaluation, ensuring fairness and transparency.

Thank you for the detailed feedback. We appreciate the chance to clarify.

Cexplorer.io has been operating independently since 2020 without treasury support. Only recently were we able to fund a V2 from Project Catalyst that will be more future-proof. This proposal is not about rescuing a failing model — it's about strengthening essential infrastructure relied on daily by developers, SPOs, and researchers.

We agree that funding only basic operations is not enough. Our proposal includes two tracks:

a) Maintenance (uptime, protocol support)
b) Meaningful enhancements (new APIs, deeper token/contract views, developer-focused tools)

On protocol changes:
We made a strategic decision over the past six months to focus on building Cexplorer V2 — a complete rebuild with a new backend and frontend that will be much more future-proof and scalable. With limited resources, we prioritized building a better long-term solution over patching the old version.

On ads:
If funded, we will minimize or remove ads during the funding period to deliver a cleaner user experience.

On future funding:
This is a transition to self-sustainability. After 18 months, we plan to introduce optional paid API plans and light sponsorships, ensuring free access to core features while sustaining operations independently.

On continuity:
We guarantee Cexplorer will remain operational and accessible for the funded period and beyond. Our team already ensures millions of requests with >99% uptime.

On uniqueness:
Cexplorer is focused on deep analytics, tokenomics, stake pool insights, and smart contract visibility — essential tools that go beyond surface-level explorers.

On maintenance and governance:
We made a strategic decision to build governance directly into Cexplorer V2, which is close to launch. Governance support is already live on staging and will be deployed to the mainnet before or during the first 3 months of funding. This ensures governance is integrated into a future-proof platform, not a temporary patch.

We fully respect that treasury funds must be used carefully. This proposal is about keeping Cardano’s developer infrastructure open, independent, and future-ready.

Thank you again for your consideration.

Thanks for raising these points — we appreciate the chance to clarify.

On pool rankings:
Cexplorer’s default rankings are based on objective metrics like pledge, cost, performance, and saturation. Users and wallets can adjust the ranking filters freely. We have never prioritized our own pools or clients. Even now you see that in native ranking our competitors are above Cardanians stake pools.

On improvements and funding:
Much of our work in the past year has gone into building Cexplorer V2 — a full backend and frontend rebuild with governance support and scalability upgrades, not just cosmetic changes.

On stake pool operations:
Cardanians operate pools, but pool operations are separate from Cexplorer’s explorer services. Furthermore, very soon Cexplorer will become it's own independent entity completely separated from Cardanians. This proposal focuses purely on maintaining and improving Cexplorer.io as open infrastructure for Cardano.

In short:

- Rankings are fair and transparent (and will be even more so in V2 btw).
- Funding supports a major upgrade, not just basic maintenance.
- Transparency and openness remain our priorities.
